Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c3): b) ADVANCING with no BEFORE/AFTER, BEFORE AFTER together, two ADVANCING phrases, ADVANCING after EOP, FROM after ADVANCING, PAGE LINES, RECORD, AT EOP twice and END-WRITE twice refused (COBOL2269/COBOL0306), bare WRITE and a file-name operand refused; c) ord, fromlit, fromfig, fromall, file, retry, lock refused; d) a FROM function-identifier (Amendment 1) and a qualified record-name compile and run; f) -1, 1.5 and PIC 9V9 COBOL2365, 0 LINES and an 18-digit zero identifier run; a) a RECORD VARYING file written FROM an ODO group reads back its lengths 3 and 10, a length 0 WRITE gives 44; e) sequential is the only organization of this format. next.reason: §1985:VII.4.7.2 is 'WRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1]', an optional {BEFORE | AFTER} ADVANCING phrase (one of them), then AT END-OF-PAGE before NOT AT END-OF-PAGE, then [END-WRITE]. Its 2023 counterpart is §2023:14.9.51.2 'Format 1 (sequential)', which §2023:14.9.51.3 SR2 ('If the organization of the write file is sequential, format 1 shall be specified') ties to sequential files; every 1985 WRITE fits it with the same meaning. But BEFORE and AFTER are now in choice indicators, so both may be written, limited only by §2023:14.9.51.3 SR17 ('The BEFORE and AFTER phrases shall not both be specified if the PAGE phrase is specified'); the end-of-page phrases may come in either order; and 'FILE file-name-1', 'FROM literal-1', the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK are added. All are refused by the 1985 format and accepted by 2023, at compile time: CHANGED.
